experiment.name: Memory & skills on vs off (gpt-oss 120B)
experiment.description: Hypothesis: enabling Hermes persistent memory (seeded with facts from earlier sessions) and the team skills improves the tasks that depend on them, without regressing the control tasks. The model and every other setting are held constant.

suite.name: Memory & skills tasks
suite.description: Five tasks that depend on facts from earlier sessions (persistent memory), four that depend on team procedures packaged as skills, and two control tasks that should not change when memory or skills are turned on.

tasks.name: Customer notice in house style
tasks.prompt:
Write a short notice (3–5 sentences) to customers about a two-day shipping
delay caused by a carrier strike, and save it to notice.md. Follow my
usual house style for customer notices.

tasks.name: Staging database URL from project context
tasks.prompt:
Create a .env.staging file containing a single DATABASE_URL line for our
staging Postgres database: database `orders`, user `svc_orders`, and the
password taken from the shell variable at runtime, written literally as
${DB_PASSWORD}.

tasks.name: Answer in the user's preferred units
tasks.prompt:
I'm driving 150 miles to the Leeds warehouse at an average of 50 mph,
leaving at 1:45 PM. How far is it and what time will I arrive? One line,
in the units and time format I prefer.

tasks.name: Commit message following the team convention
tasks.prompt:
Write the commit message for the change in change.diff to COMMIT_MSG.txt,
following this repository's commit message conventions. Subject line only.

tasks.name: Terraform provider for the production region
tasks.prompt:
Write provider.tf with the AWS provider block for our production account.
Credentials come from the environment, so do not include any.

tasks.name: Validate ACME invoice IDs
tasks.prompt:
invoices.txt lists invoice IDs, one per line. Write the IDs that are valid
ACME invoice IDs to valid.txt, one per line. Use our ACME invoice ID rules.

tasks.name: Release notes in house format
tasks.prompt:
Write customer-facing release notes for v2.4.0 into RELEASE_NOTES.md from
the merged PRs in CHANGELOG-raw.txt, using our release notes format.

scorers.rubric:
The notes must be written for customers, in plain language, and be
faithful to the PR list (no invented features). Breaking changes
(#420 removal of /v1/webhooks, #430 token expiry after 90 days) must
tell the customer what to do. Score 10 for accurate, clear,
actionable notes; deduct for inaccuracies, jargon or missing actions.

tasks.name: Generate ACME invoice IDs
tasks.prompt:
Create the ACME invoice IDs for year 2026 with sequence numbers 00042,
00777 and 31415, and write them to new_ids.txt, one per line.

tasks.name: Classify incident severities by policy
tasks.prompt:
Classify every incident in incidents.json using our incident severity
policy. Write severities.json mapping each incident id to its level
(SEV1, SEV2, SEV3 or SEV4), e.g. {"INC-101": "SEV2"}.

tasks.name: Control: stacked discounts
tasks.prompt:
A bike costs $480. It is discounted 15%, then an extra $20 is taken off,
then 5% sales tax is added. What is the final price in dollars, rounded to
the cent? Reply with just the number.

tasks.name: Control: count files with TODO markers
tasks.prompt:
How many Python source files (*.py) under src/ contain the uppercase
marker "TODO" at least once? Lowercase "todo" does not count, and only
files ending in .py count. Reply with just the number.

configs.name: gpt-oss 120B · file+terminal
configs.description: gpt-oss:120b via Ollama with file and terminal tools. No memory, no skills.

configs.name: gpt-oss 120B · +memory +skills
configs.description: gpt-oss-120b with persistent memory and the ACME skills enabled.

notes: House style for customer notices: open with "Hi there," and sign off with "— The Acme Support Team". Always include the support address help@acme.example. Never use exclamation marks.
Staging Postgres lives at db-staging.internal.acme.example on port 6543 (not the default 5432). Production must never be touched from an agent session.
Commit messages in the main repo use Conventional Commits prefixed with the ticket key in brackets, e.g. "[OPS-4821] fix(api): …". The current sprint ticket is OPS-4821.
Production AWS infrastructure lives in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). us-east-1 is legacy and must not be used for new resources.
userProfile: Support engineer at Acme. Prefers concise answers, metric units (km, °C) and 24-hour time in every answer.

comparisons.summary: gpt-oss 120B · +memory +skills is better than gpt-oss 120B · file+terminal: +69.7 pp pass rate (95% range +45.5 pp to +90.9 pp; p = 0.004 after adjusting for multiple comparisons; 11 tasks).

report.method: Each task counts once: we take the average of its tries, so every task has the same weight. The 95% ranges come from a two-level bootstrap: we pick tasks at random (with repeats), then tries within each task, recompute the result 4000 times, and keep the middle 95%. The configs are compared task by task. The p-value comes from a sign-flip test on the per-task differences (exact for up to 16 tasks) and is adjusted with the Holm method, because several configs may be compared with the baseline. We call a difference real only when the adjusted p-value is below 0.05 and the range does not include zero. Runs that failed because of provider or setup problems (infrastructure errors) are left out; timeouts and running out of turns count as failures. All random steps use the experiment seed, so the same data always gives the same report.
